answer: A river of agent payments only stays clean when every identity must lock a bond before it can transact, the way water is forced through a narrow canyon: each new agent deposits funds that stay frozen while it works, and the deposit is its relic of good behaviour. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds, and any identity caught cheating loses its bond to honest peers — fraud ends up costing more than it can earn.
